title: Dependency outage: one caller spins while its siblings stay flat

problem.summary: A dependency is stopped, and the ONE service that calls it starts spinning on retries. No new container appears - this fault removes a container rather than adding one - so the newcomer route cannot find it. The signature is a syscall storm confined to a single existing container.
symptoms: requests through one path fail or hang rather than slowing
one service's resource use rises sharply while its peers do not
a dependency produces little or no traffic

discriminators.signal: getrusage rate in a single container, against its identical siblings
discriminators.this_problem: one java container goes from 5.3/s to 2,474-2,701/s while three other java containers stay at 6.7/s (n=2 runs)
discriminators.not_this_problem: a host-wide fault moves every container together. If the siblings move too, this is not it
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). MEASURED with blueprints/lib/who_makes_it.py on dependency_outage r1 and r2: getrusage 5.3/s -> 2474.1/s and 5.3 -> 2700.9 in pid_ns 4026533460, with the other three java namespaces at 6.7/s in both runs. 100% of the change is application processes, 0% the harness.

discriminators.signal: no container is new to the window
discriminators.this_problem: none. This fault stops an existing container; across every run measured, the newcomer search returns nothing
discriminators.not_this_problem: every other fault family we measured injects a sidecar container, so a newcomer is present
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). fault_fingerprint.py reports 'no newcomer container found' for every dependency_outage run, while finding one in all five runs of each of six other families.

discriminators.signal: new outbound socket binds in the caller
discriminators.not_this_problem: bind stays within 1.1-1.6x in every other family
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). bind x7.3 for dependency_outage against x1.1-1.6 for all seven other families in the specificity sweep.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the stopped dependency can be named directly from the kernel trace
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: a stopped container simply stops producing events. Absence is not distinguishable from a container that was always idle without knowing the topology, and a kernel trace carries no service names.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: name the SPINNING container and say its dependency is unreachable. Identifying which dependency needs spans, logs or a topology map.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: getrusage is the mechanism rather than an artefact of this runtime
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: measured on two Sock Shop runs, both Java callers. Whether a Go or Node caller produces the same storm was not tested.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: treat the SHAPE - one container's syscall rate exploding while identical siblings stay flat - as the discriminator, and the specific syscall as a Java detail.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: a verdict naming the container and the mechanism, or an explicit abstain
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: a container is new to the window
its share profile matches the measured range below
no sibling container shows the same profile

rule_out.when: a container IS new to the window - this fault removes a container, it does not add one
every container moved together rather than one moving alone

decision.root_cause_is: the stopped dependency. The container that spins is the VICTIM, and naming it as the culprit is the mistake this blueprint exists to prevent

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Built 22-09-2026 from blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py over 41 labelled runs of 8 families. Candidate signals were first put through discover_signature.py (a specificity sweep across families, which rejected unlinkat, ftruncate, block_split, lseek and dup as window artefacts) and who_makes_it.py (which rejected the nagle_delayed_ack host-wide signal as 94% our own load generator). KERNEL TRACES ONLY - no metrics, logs or spans were consulted.

apply_when: requests through one path fail or hang rather than slowing
one service's activity rises sharply while its peers do not
no new container appeared during the window
do_not_apply_when: a new container appeared - use the newcomer blueprints instead
every container moved together, which is host-wide
applicability.cheap_precheck: one container's syscall rate rose roughly a hundredfold while containers running the same image did not move

stopping_conditions.conclude: the share profile matches and no sibling container matches it too
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: a discriminating share falls outside its measured range
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container is new to the window and none stands out

applicable_symptoms: requests through one path fail or hang rather than slowing
one service's resource use rises sharply while its peers do not
a dependency produces little or no traffic

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the shares and say which blueprint they sit between
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the container's shares and every sibling's, side by side
